column1: # boru Language Specification: Word Modifiers (the /… suffix)
# An unquoted word may carry a `/…` modifier suffix. The recognised
#   /f   force-forward : collect ALL args from forward tokens
#   /s   force-stack   : collect ALL args from the prefix stack
#   /N   arg-count     : a digit run; select the overload with N total args
#   /q   quote         : parse the word as an Atom (data, not a call)
#   /r   ref           : resolve a fn word to its Function value, uninvoked
#   /u   usurp         : wrap a fn with its argument order reversed
#   - letters may appear in ANY order  (foo/sq ≡ foo/qs, foo/ur ≡ foo/ru)
#   - each letter appears AT MOST once  (no /ff, /ss, /qq, /rr, /uu)
#   - f and s are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE
#   - q is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with r and with u
#   - digits form a SINGLE contiguous run
#   - any other letter, or a forbidden pairing, is INVALID
# Precedence when valid: q dominates (yields an Atom; f/s/digit ignored);
# r and u yield reference / usurp words (f/s/digit accepted but ignored,
# An INVALID suffix splits by its spelling (NUR027 — previously every
# invalid suffix silently became a plain word, surfacing later as an
#   - spelled ENTIRELY from the modifier alphabet (digits + f s q r u t):
#     a botched modifier, never a legitimate name — a LOUD parse error
#   - containing any NON-modifier character (uppercase included): the
#     whole token (slash and all) stays a single plain word — that is
#     what keeps slash-bearing names (`add/x`) and the builtin type
# Full coverage of /r and /u lives in ref.tsv and usurp.tsv; this file is
# the modifier matrix — every variation and combination, including errors.
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  sub2/f 10 3

column3: all args from the prefix stack
